cards.text: This is a song of David, Israel's future king, written for the choirmaster to the tune of "Do Not Destroy." The heading says it comes from when David fled from Saul, king of Israel, into a cave. Cold rock all around him, and David starts to pray.

cards.question: David begs God to have mercy on him, and he says his soul takes refuge in ___.

cards.text: Then David says he'll take shelter in the shadow of God's wings. Me? When I got scared back in that junk drawer, I hid under a warranty card, so David is doing MUCH better than I did.

cards.question: David says he'll take shelter in the shadow of God's wings. How long does he plan to stay there?
David cries out to God Most High. What does David say God does for him?
David is crying out from a cave. True or false: David says God reaches down from heaven and saves him.
David says God rebukes the ones who trample him. And what does David say God sends forth?

answers.text: His loving devotion and His truth

cards.text: Then David says his soul is among the lions, and he lies down with ravenous beasts. And I thought I had it rough sharing a junk drawer with a pile of dead batteries!

cards.question: David says he lies down with ravenous beasts. But these beasts are really ___, whose teeth are spears and arrows and whose tongues are sharp swords.

cards.text: And right there, in the middle of all that, David stops talking about the lions. He starts talking to God.

cards.question: In the middle of the danger, what does David pray?

answers.text: That God be exalted above the heavens
That Saul would be struck down
That the cave would stay hidden

cards.question: They spread a net for David's feet, and his soul was despondent. They dug a pit in front of him too. True or false: the ones who dug the pit fall into it themselves.

cards.text: They dug a pit for David and fell in it THEMSELVES. That's like rigging a prank on your coworker's chair and then sitting down in it yourself.

cards.question: David tells God his heart is ___, and he says it twice.

cards.text: David also says he'll sing and make music. He even calls out to his instruments: "Awake, O harp and lyre!"

cards.question: David is ready to sing and make music. What does he say he will awaken?

cards.text: Most of us hit snooze when the sun comes up. David? David is out here being the alarm clock for the SUN!

cards.question: True or false: David says he'll keep his praise private, away from the nations.
David gives his reason for singing God's praises among the peoples. How high does he say God's loving devotion reaches?

cards.text: And God's faithfulness reaches to the clouds. Then David closes with that line again: "Be exalted, O God, above the heavens; may Your glory cover all the earth."

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'the cave' can be argued as right. Card 1 says David fled into a cave, and the Psalm 57:1 heading says the same. Fleeing into a cave is taking refuge there, so a baker could defend 'his soul takes refuge in the cave.'

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: The joke adds a new detail to Papa Dorin's backstory: that he got scared in the junk drawer and hid under a warranty card. The backstory never says this. Jokes may make up small moments around his bakery, not new events from the drawer.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: 'He starts talking to God' says David turns to God for the first time at verse 5. That isn't true. David already speaks to God directly in verse 1 ('Have mercy on me, O God'). Verse 5 is a return to speaking to God, not a start.

rule.text: Noticing: What he points out must be true.

findings.problem: The question opens with 'They spread a net for David's feet' but never says who 'they' are. 'They' points back to the men in card 9, which the baker can no longer see.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: This story card only repeats Psalm 57:6, which card 12 just asked about (the diggers fall into their own pit), and then adds a joke. It tells nothing new, so it's a recap card. The joke should ride on a card that moves the passage forward.
This story card only repeats Psalm 57:8 (awakening the dawn), which card 16 just asked about, and then adds a joke. It doesn't move the baker forward in the passage, so it's a recap card.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: Card 1 states facts from outside the passage ('David, Israel's future king' and 'Saul, king of Israel'), but the card cites only Psalm 57:1. prep-walkthrough.md says outside facts are fine 'with their reference,' and papa-dorin.md says every Bible fact carries its reference. But the story card's 'verses' field must cite only the passage verses the card tells, and the 'New people' example ('Cyrus, king of Persia') shows no reference.
findings.question: When a card names who a new person is using a fact from outside the passage, where does that fact's reference go? Options: in the card text, in an extra field, or not needed for a short 'who they are' description?
